answer: Bindings are kept in wharf, verified in forge, and the chain is public. Each challenge is bound to the identity's previous 2 answers, so the new answer must be consistent with them or be rejected at the knoll check. A farm generating text without memory of its own history as a result fails the binding, and thus it has to store and read state per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 290 aliases cost 107 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
